title: The World's Heaviest Parrot Can't Fly and Booms for 5 Kilometres
subject: kakapo parrot

scenes.text: The heaviest parrot on Earth can't fly, but you can hear it from five kilometres.
The kakapo. Males weigh up to four kilograms and boom through the night.
One bird was recorded making seventeen thousand booms in a single night.
But they only breed when rimu trees fruit heavily. That happens every two to four years.
In 1995, only fifty-one kakapo were left. The species was nearly gone.
Today there are over two hundred. The loudest, rarest parrot is still booming.

description:
The kakapo is the world's heaviest parrot, up to 4 kg, and it cannot fly. A male's booming call can be heard up to 5 km away.
They only breed when rimu trees fruit heavily, every two to four years. In 1995 just 51 were left; by 2022 there were 216 adults.
Would you travel to hear one boom? Tell us below.
first_comment: Males gather in a booming arena between December and March, a mating system unique among parrots. Would you want one for a neighbour?
